endorsements.quote: Ensuring AI models are suitable for rural Australian healthcare systems requires rigorous validation studies using local datasets before implementation.
Subgroup analyses should be conducted at all stages to ensure equitable AI performance across different patient populations and to monitor its impact on health equity.
Furthermore, there is a risk of bias when developing these models; therefore, monitoring and re-evaluation should include subgroup analyses.
Although it is difficult to provide general timelines, annual checks may provide sufficient monitoring for many of these AI models.
Ultimately, AI implementation should demonstrate tangible improvements in patient‐ or system‐centred outcomes.

unlisted_practices: Incorporate backup measures so AI services continue during connectivity disruptions.
Maintain human oversight and manual intervention so essential functions continue if AI tools become unavailable.
Involve rural community members and healthcare staff in AI design, development, and rollout to build trust and acceptance.
Ensure datasets used for AI in rural areas are sufficiently large and anonymised to avoid reidentification.
Engage diverse stakeholders throughout AI development, testing, and evaluation to prevent perpetuating disparities.
Ensure auditing systems and processes exist to evaluate declining model performance and guide when to re-derive the model.
Use AI as an adjunct to, not a replacement for, standard clinical care.
Perform post-implementation monitoring of adverse effects of AI tools.
Evolve rural-based AI governance frameworks to ensure equitable, context-appropriate oversight.
Developers of AI models in metropolitan centres should consider adaptability to rural settings and ensure training datasets account for smaller populations and diverse needs.
Use multiple performance metrics and large sample sizes in local validation studies.

screen.reason: This is a commentary/perspective article discussing challenges and recommendations for deploying AI and LLMs in rural Australian healthcare settings.
